Basic Information for CVE-2026-77339 Vulnerability Information Process Compose: Browser DNS rebinding lets websites control local process-compose MCP tools Overview An unauthorized access vulnerability exists in the MCP SSE listener in Process Compose. When MCP SSE is enabled, a malicious website can access the loopback listener using the DNS Rebinding technique, thereby interacting with the local service via the MCP protocol. Affected Versions Affected versions: All versions prior to Process Compose 1.120.0 Fixed version: Process Compose 1.120.0 Details Vulnerability Location: The MCP SSE listener in src/mcp/server.go. Root Cause: When the listener accepts browser-initiated requests to the /sse and message endpoints, it does not validate the Host header, does not validate the Origin header, and does not authenticate the caller. Attack Vector: A malicious website leverages DNS Rebinding to resolve a domain to a local loopback address (Loopback). The browser initiates an MCP request to the local listener. If expose_control_tools is enabled, an attacker can perform the following operations: Enumerate process status Read or search logs Truncate logs Start, stop, restart, or scale local processes User-defined custom tools may expose additional commands and outputs Lack of Protection: The Token middleware for the Gin REST API does not protect this independently started MCP listener.
